ko.R: 이제 내가 여러분에게 쓰는 것은 이것입니다. 믿는 사람이라고 하면서도 성적인 죄를 짓거나, 욕심이 많거나, 우상을 섬기거나, 남에게 욕하거나, 술에 취하거나, 남을 속이는 사람이 있으면, 그런 사람과는 어울리지 마십시오. 그런 사람과는 함께 밥을 먹지도 마십시오.

pt.L: Mas agora escrevo a vocês que não se misturem [com alguém], se alguém que se diz {{gender:irmão ou irmã|irmão}} for sexualmente imoral, ou ganancioso, ou idólatra, ou insultador, ou beberrão, ou trapaceiro; com esse tal, nem mesmo comer.
pt.B: Mas o que escrevo a vocês agora é isto: fiquem longe de qualquer um que se diga {{gender:irmão ou irmã|irmão}} e, no entanto, seja sexualmente imoral, ganancioso, idólatra, insultador, beberrão ou trapaceiro. Com alguém assim, não se sentem nem mesmo para comer.
pt.R: Agora estou escrevendo para dizer isto: não andem com alguém que faz parte da igreja, mas comete pecados sexuais ou é ganancioso, ou adora ídolos, insulta as pessoas, se embriaga ou engana os outros. Nem comam com uma pessoa assim.

am.L: አሁን ግን እጽፍላችኋለሁ፤ {{gender:ወንድም ወይም እኅት|ወንድም}} እየተባለ ሴሰኛ ወይም ስግብግብ ወይም ጣዖት አምላኪ ወይም ተሳዳቢ ወይም ሰካራም ወይም አጭበርባሪ ከሆነ ሰው ጋር እንዳትደባለቁ፤ ከእንደዚህ ዓይነቱ ጋር አብራችሁ እንኳ እንዳትበሉ።
am.B: አሁን ግን የምጽፍላችሁ ይህ ነው፦ {{gender:ወንድም ወይም እኅት|ወንድም}} እየተባለ ሴሰኛ፣ ስግብግብ፣ ጣዖት አምላኪ፣ ተሳዳቢ፣ ሰካራም ወይም አጭበርባሪ ከሆነ ማንኛውም ሰው ራቁ። ከእንደዚህ ዓይነቱ ሰው ጋር ለመብላት እንኳ አትቀመጡ።
am.R: አሁን የምጽፍላችሁ ይህን ለመንገር ነው፦ አማኝ ተብሎ እየታወቀ የፆታ ኃጢአት ከሚፈጽም ወይም ስግብግብ ከሆነ፣ ወይም ጣዖትን ከሚያመልክ፣ ሰዎችን ከሚሰድብ፣ ከሚሰክር ወይም ሌሎችን ከሚያታልል ሰው ጋር ጊዜ አታሳልፉ። ከእንደዚህ ዓይነቱ ሰው ጋር ምግብ እንኳ አትብሉ።

ru.L: Теперь же я пишу вам не смешиваться [ни с кем], если кто, называясь {{gender:братом или сестрой|братом}}, будет блудником, или жадным, или идолопоклонником, или злоречивым, или пьяницей, или грабителем; с таким даже не есть вместе.
ru.B: А теперь я пишу вам вот что: держитесь подальше от всякого, кто называет себя {{gender:братом или сестрой|братом}}, а сам — распутник, жадный, идолопоклонник, злоречивый, пьяница или мошенник. С таким человеком даже не садитесь за стол.

uk.L: А тепер я написав вам не єднатися, якщо хтось, що зветься {{gender:братом чи сестрою|братом}}, є розпусником, чи жадібним, чи ідолопоклонником, чи лихословом, чи пʼяницею, чи здирником; з таким навіть не їсти.
uk.B: А тепер я пишу вам ось що: не водіться з тим, хто зветься {{gender:братом чи сестрою|братом}}, а сам є розпусником, жадібним, ідолопоклонником, лихословом, пʼяницею чи здирником. З такою людиною навіть не сідайте їсти.
uk.R: Тепер я пишу вам ось що: не проводьте часу з тим, кого знають як вірного, але хто чинить статеві гріхи, чи жадібний, чи поклоняється ідолам, чи ображає людей, чи напивається, чи обманює інших. З такою людиною навіть не їжте разом.

ja.L: しかし今、わたしはあなたがたに書きます。{{gender:きょうだい|兄弟}}と呼ばれている者で、淫らな者、貪欲な者、偶像礼拝者、人をののしる者、酒に酔う者、だまし取る者がいるなら、交わってはいけません。そのような者とは、いっしょに食事をしてもいけません。
ja.B: しかし今、わたしが書いているのはこういうことです。{{gender:きょうだい|兄弟}}と呼ばれていながら、淫らな者、貪欲な者、偶像礼拝者、人をののしる者、酒に酔う者、だまし取る者である人がいれば、その人と付き合ってはいけません。そういう人とは、いっしょに食事をすることさえしてはいけません。
ja.R: 今わたしが書いているのは、こういうことです。信仰の仲間だと言われていながら、性的な罪を犯す人、欲ばりな人、偶像を拝む人、人の悪口を言う人、酔っぱらう人、人をだます人がいたら、そういう人と付き合わないでください。そういう人とは、いっしょに食事をすることもしないでください。

decisions.choice: now I write: Paul is writing this now, to make his meaning clear
alternatives: what I actually wrote (in the earlier letter) was this
decisions.reason: ἔγραψα has the same form as in verse 9. Letter writers could use this past tense for the letter they were writing, since it would be past when read (as in Philemon 19, 21). With "now" set against verse 9, Paul gives his instruction afresh. It may instead mean "I meant": what the earlier letter said. The instruction is the same either way.

decisions.choice: called a brother: a church member, someone known as a fellow believer
alternatives: someone falsely claiming to be a believer
decisions.reason: ὀνομαζόμενος means "named, bearing the name". Paul means anyone who belongs to the church and bears the name of brother or sister, whatever his life shows. The word is masculine, as Greek usage required for anyone, but Paul's rule applies to men and women alike.

decisions.choice: abusive: one who insults and reviles others; drunkard: one given to drunkenness
decisions.reason: λοίδορος is one who heaps abuse on others with words; μέθυσος is one who habitually gets drunk. These two are added to the list of verse 10, perhaps because they were problems in the church (compare 11:21). For the other words see 5:10.

decisions.choice: not even to eat with: no shared meals, which in that culture expressed fellowship, and so not the Lord's Supper either
decisions.reason: To eat together was a sign of acceptance and friendship (Galatians 2:12). The church's common meals included the Lord's Supper (11:20-22), so Paul's words exclude the man from the church's table. The aim, as verse 5 shows, is his repentance and rescue.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}
decisions.reason: The rule covers any church member, women and men (m2). Readable says "fellow believer", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: sexually immoral, greedy, idolater, abusive, drunkard, swindler (L, B); commits sexual sins, is greedy, worships idols, insults people, gets drunk, cheats others (R)
decisions.reason: The four words from verse 10 keep the same English. "Abusive" is chosen over "reviler", which is old-fashioned, and over "slanderer", which is narrower: one who speaks against others behind their backs.

decisions.choice: {{gender:frère ou sœur|frère}} (L, B); quelqu’un qui se dit croyant (R)
decisions.reason: As in English, the rule covers any church member (m2). Readable says "someone who calls himself a believer" with the generic "quelqu’un", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: injurieux, ivrogne (L, B); qui insulte les gens, qui s’enivre (R)
decisions.reason: "Injurieux" is the usual adjective for one who abuses others in words; "médisant" and "calomniateur" are narrower, as the English decision says of "slanderer". The same words return in 6:10.

decisions.choice: hermano, no setting
decisions.reason: As in Romans 14:10, Spanish "hermano" for a fellow believer covers a man or a woman, so the English setting ({{gender:brother or sister|brother}}) has no Spanish span; the adjectives of the list agree with it in the ordinary generic form. Readable says "creyente", as the English Readable says "fellow believer".

decisions.choice: ndugu, no gender span
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means a brother or a sister, so the English gender span has nothing to switch in Swahili.

decisions.choice: mtukanaji, mlevi (L, B); anawatukana watu, analewa (R)
decisions.reason: The two words this list adds to 5:10, in the same pattern: a noun for the person at Literal and Balanced, a verb for what the person does at Readable.

decisions.choice: {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} (L, B) for a singular adelphos meaning any believer; "một tín hữu" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Romans 14:10 and 1 Thessalonians 4:6: the gender span carries the Greek word; Readable says "a believer", which is already for men and women.

decisions.choice: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} for the singular "brother" meaning any believer (L, B); "믿는 사람" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Romans 14:10 and 1 Thessalonians 4:6, a believer named by the word "brother" takes the gender setting, since the person may be a woman; Readable says "fellow believer".

decisions.choice: insultador; beberrão
decisions.reason: For the whole book, the two words that join the list here (see verse 10): "insultador" for one who abuses others with words (m3), wider than "caluniador", which is one who lies about others; "beberrão" for one given to drink. Readable says "insulta as pessoas" and "se embriaga".

decisions.choice: {{gender:ወንድም ወይም እኅት|ወንድም}} (brother or sister / brother)
decisions.reason: "Brother" here means any church member, woman or man, so the inclusive form is the default, as in the English and as the book's terms note sets for the singular.

decisions.choice: {{gender:भाई या बहन|भाई}}
decisions.reason: The rule covers any church member, women and men (meaning decision m2); Hindi uses the style guide's singular span. Readable says "साथी विश्वासी", which needs no setting, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "गाली देनेवाला", "पियक्कड़" (L, B); "लोगों का अपमान करता है", "नशे में धुत रहता है" (R)
decisions.reason: The two words added to the list of verse 10 (meaning decision m3), in the same pattern as the rest.

decisions.choice: {{gender:братом или сестрой|братом}}
decisions.reason: The gender setting, as in the English: the rule covers any church member, women and men (m2). Readable says "верующим", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: злоречивым (L, B); оскорбляет людей (R)
decisions.reason: The word is for one who insults and reviles others (m3); "сквернослов" would mean only foul language.

decisions.choice: you judge those inside: the church is responsible for the conduct of its own members
decisions.reason: οὐχὶ asks a question that expects "yes": it is the church's task to judge its own. Paul has just done so in verses 3-5, and he tells them to act in verse 13. He returns to the church's judging in 6:1-6.

decisions.choice: judges: God is the judge of those outside, now and at the end
alternatives: will judge: a future tense, pointing to the final judgment
decisions.reason: The Greek letters of κρίνει can be read as present ("judges") or future ("will judge"); the difference lies only in the accent, which the earliest manuscripts do not mark. The SBLGNT accents it as present. Either way God, not the church, is the judge of outsiders, and the final judgment is in view (4:5).

decisions.choice: Are not those inside the ones you are to judge, while God judges those outside? (B); statements (R)
alternatives: Do you not judge those inside, but those outside God judges?
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the question but puts it in natural order; Readable turns it into two statements, as the question expects agreement, and names the church.

ja.B: あなたがたの中から、悪を行う者を除き去りなさい。

decisions.choice: a refrain from Deuteronomy, used of removing a person who has done evil from Israel
alternatives: Paul's own words, with no allusion
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy repeats this command after laws about serious sins (Deuteronomy 17:7; 19:19; 22:21, 24; 24:7), and in the Greek Old Testament it is worded almost exactly as here, with the verb in the singular. Paul makes it plural, a command to the whole church. Deuteronomy 22:30 (23:1 in the Hebrew), which forbids a man to take his father's wife, stands in the same chapter. Paul gives no formula such as "it is written"; he takes Scripture's words as his own command.

decisions.choice: the evil one: the person who has done evil, here the man of verse 1
decisions.reason: πονηρὸν with the masculine article means an evil person, as in Deuteronomy. In other places the same words can mean the devil (Matthew 13:19), but here they apply to the man living with his father's wife.

decisions.choice: drive out: remove from the community
decisions.reason: In Deuteronomy the evildoer was put to death. Paul applies the words to the church's discipline: the man is to be put out of the fellowship (verses 2, 5, 11), not harmed.

decisions.choice: Do what the Scriptures command: (R)
decisions.reason: Readable tells the reader that the words come from Scripture (m1), which a reader of the Greek Old Testament would hear. Literal and Balanced, like the Greek, give no introduction or quotation marks.

decisions.choice: the evildoer (B)
decisions.reason: "The evil one" would suggest the devil in English (m2). "Evildoer" names a person who has done evil and needs no gender setting.

decisions.choice: celui qui fait le mal (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Malfaiteur" means a criminal in modern French, and "le méchant" (kept at Literal) can sound childish. "Celui qui fait le mal" names the person who has done evil (m2), with the generic "celui qui" and no setting.

decisions.choice: "các ngươi" (R) inside the quotation from Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: Where Readable makes the quotation explicit, God's command to Israel keeps the form God uses in the law ("các ngươi"), as in the Vietnamese Romans; Literal and Balanced keep Paul's own "anh chị em".

decisions.choice: Readable sets the command as a quotation of Deuteronomy in the plain style, with "너희"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the words as the refrain of Deuteronomy; the English Readable names Scripture, so the Korean Readable quotes it in the plain style of quoted Scripture, as Romans does.

decisions.choice: "कुकर्मी"
decisions.reason: The evil one is the person who has done evil (meaning decision m2); "कुकर्मी" names an evildoer and cannot be taken for the devil.

decisions.choice: злодея
decisions.reason: "Лукавый" would suggest the devil; the sense is the person who has done evil (m2).

decisions.choice: злого (L); лиходія (B)
decisions.reason: The evil one is the person who did the evil of verse 1 (m2). "Лукавий" as a noun is heard in Ukrainian as the devil, so Literal keeps the plain adjective "злий"; Balanced says "лиходій", the evildoer.
